solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Business is secure in refuge (7,6)

blocks.note: to land a deal or a fish is to secure it

annotation.surface: A company hides away from the world somewhere safe.
annotation.walkthrough: A traffic island is the raised strip in the middle of a road where pedestrians can wait safely, hence a refuge. 'Secure' reads as an adjective but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A traffic island is literally called a refuge in British road terminology.

entries.clue: Broadcast each little play on psychic channel (14)

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are strewn about

annotation.surface: A radio station airs every short drama on a channel devoted to the paranormal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'channel' together make the clue sound like television scheduling, hiding that 'Broadcast' is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Communicating telepathically is sending thoughts by a psychic channel rather than speech.

entries.clue: Warning signal is a gong, right? (5)

blocks.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour; the MBE is a British one (Member of the Order of the British Empire)

annotation.surface: Someone checks whether striking a gong counts as raising the alarm.
annotation.walkthrough: The gong looks like a noise-maker for a warning, but it is the British slang for an honour, and the MBE is the standard crossword gong.
annotation.definitionFit: The amber traffic light warns that the signal is about to change.

entries.clue: Race, leaning over and dropping in the wrong place (3-7)

annotation.surface: A runner stumbles mid-race, tilting and falling in the wrong spot.
annotation.walkthrough: Fly-tipping is the British term for illegally dumping rubbish, such as old mattresses by the roadside.
annotation.definitionFit: Fly-tipping is dumping waste where it should not go, literally dropping it in the wrong place.

entries.clue: Heart of sanctum violated given special protection (7)

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: C is the fourth of SANCTUM's seven letters

annotation.surface: The inner sanctuary, once desecrated, is now placed under special guard.
annotation.walkthrough: A charmed life is one protected as if by a spell.
annotation.definitionFit: Something charmed is guarded by magic, given special protection against harm.

entries.clue: Small section of cake executive eats (7)

indicators.note: the suit takes the bun inside it, as a mouth takes food

blocks.note: a suit is slang for a business executive
a bun is a small cake

annotation.surface: A manager helps himself to a slice of the office cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a slice of cake; 'Small section of cake' is not a unit at all, since 'of' joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A subunit is a smaller unit within a larger organisation, a small section of it.

entries.clue: Turner cut round back of panel (4)

indicators.note: the axe goes round the L, enclosing it
the back of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: The painter J. M. W. Turner trims around the rear of a picture panel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turner' with its capital looks like the painter; here it is anything that turns, and an axle turns wheels.
annotation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod on which a wheel turns, or which turns itself.

entries.clue: Study Renaissance artist’s sound teeth (9)

indicators.note: the artist's name is only to be said, not spelt

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

annotation.surface: An art student examines the healthy teeth in a Renaissance portrait.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like praise of healthy teeth, but it says the artist's name is heard rather than read.
annotation.definitionFit: Dentition is the arrangement of the teeth, the teeth taken as a set.

entries.clue: Often, wellbeing results from cooking this rich food (4,10)

indicators.note: to cook is to tamper with, as in cooking the books

annotation.surface: A health tip: feeling well comes from cooking this hearty dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the fodder is what comes out when the answer is cooked, so the letters of the dish rearrange into 'Often, wellbeing'.
annotation.definitionFit: Beef Wellington is fillet steak baked in pastry with pâté, a famously rich dish.

entries.clue: Chuck book back in library corridor (5)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: Someone tosses a library book back out into the hallway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book back' sounds like returning a book or reversing it; the back belongs to 'library' instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A lobby is a hall or corridor, especially an entrance passage.

entries.clue: Flashy vehicle regularly involved in accidents (9)

definitions.text: Flashy vehicle regularly involved in accidents

blocks.note: the surface wants a showy car; the setter means a vehicle with flashing lights on its roof
the surface wants a reckless driver; the setter means a vehicle whose routine work is attending crashes

annotation.surface: A showy sports car that keeps crashing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flashy' suggests a show-off car and 'involved in accidents' a bad driver; an ambulance flashes its lights and attends accidents as its job.
annotation.definitionFit: An ambulance has flashing blue lights and turns up at accidents routinely.

entries.clue: Diet of mother possibly bearing Irishman’s son? (10)

indicators.note: the parent carries the name inside, as a mother bears a child

blocks.note: a mother is one example of a parent
Liam is a typical Irish boy's name, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: An Irish family's food: what the mother ate while carrying her son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diet' with a capital looks like food but is an assembly, as in the Japanese Diet; the question mark flags Liam as just one example of an Irish son.
annotation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal legislative assembly, which is what a parliament is.

entries.clue: Half of rabble repeated notes (4)

indicators.note: keep only one half of the word

blocks.note: rabble = RIFFRAFF; keep the first half

annotation.surface: Half the mob chanted the same notes over and over.
annotation.walkthrough: The rabble must first become RIFFRAFF before it can be halved.
annotation.definitionFit: A riff is a short phrase of notes repeated in jazz or rock.

entries.clue: City urchin is hot stuff (10)

blocks.note: a brat is an unruly child, an urchin

annotation.surface: A street kid from the city is a real firebrand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' reads as praise of the urchin; it is lava, molten rock.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by category: the capital of Slovakia, on the Danube, is simply named as a city.

entries.clue: Tricked, go back to capture pawn (7)

indicators.note: the word for 'go' is read backwards
the reversed word takes the pawn inside it

annotation.surface: A chess player, fooled, retreats a piece to take a pawn.
annotation.walkthrough: The chess picture of moving back to take a pawn hides that 'back' reverses DEPART.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone lured into a snare by deceit has been fooled, both past participles.

entries.clue: Lower oneself, rolling round in rotten manure: it conveys immunity (9)

indicators.note: the word turns over, so it reads backwards
the turned word goes inside the rearranged letters
rotten = spoilt, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to sit is to lower oneself into a seat

annotation.surface: Someone wallows in rotting dung, claiming it will make them immune.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'rolling round in' as wallowing in muck; it is really two instructions, a turn and then an insertion into the jumbled letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An antiserum is blood serum carrying antibodies, which passes on immunity.

entries.clue: Destructive little creature: call it home at last (7)

indicators.note: take only the final letter of 'home'

annotation.surface: A naughty child is finally told to call home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Call it home' sounds like settling down somewhere; termites do exactly that, eating the house they live in.
annotation.definitionFit: Termites are small insects that destroy wooden buildings.

entries.clue: Chants relax tension (7)

indicators.note: loosen the word so its letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: Meditative chanting helps to release stress.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is sound advice about chanting to unwind, which hides the anagram well.
annotation.definitionFit: To intone is to chant in a steady monotone.

entries.clue: Official in force shoots up, injecting heroin (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means read from bottom to top
the H is pushed inside the reversed letters, like a needle

blocks.note: to shoot a gun = to fire it

annotation.surface: A police officer takes drugs by needle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoots up' reads as injecting drugs, but it is FIRES written upwards. F and FIRES are reversed together as SERIFF before the H goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the county lawman of the American West, or the Crown's officer in a British shire, holds a public office.

entries.clue: Honest about element of visual receptivity (7)

indicators.note: the word for honest wraps round the element

annotation.surface: A candid remark on the eye's capacity to take in light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Element of visual receptivity' reads as one phrase, but 'element' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Retinal means relating to the retina, the part of the eye that receives light.

entries.clue: Viewer about to hold annual test for wireless devices (7)

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'about turn': the soldier faces the other way, so the word is read backwards
the turned word holds the test inside it

blocks.note: a seer is one who sees
the MOT is the yearly roadworthiness test for British cars

annotation.surface: A TV viewer is about to run the yearly check on cordless gadgets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' sounds like a TV watcher reaching for the remote, but it is SEER, turned round by 'about'.
annotation.definitionFit: Remotes are handheld devices that control a TV without wires.

entries.clue: A band item (4)

blocks.note: the London Symphony Orchestra, a band of musicians

annotation.surface: A single entry in a band's list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Item' is used in its old sense of 'likewise', introducing each entry in a list, which is what 'also' does.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Item' was once used before each entry in a list, meaning also or likewise.

entries.clue: Russian city is, in different ways, working OK (10)

indicators.note: 'is' is written once one way and once the other

blocks.note: Perm, a city in the Urals

annotation.surface: A Russian city is said to be functioning fine, in various respects.
annotation.walkthrough: OK is the noun here, as in 'give the OK'.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: the go-ahead, a green light, a sign-off from whoever is in charge.

entries.clue: I spoil one type of porcelain (5)

annotation.surface: A collector confesses to damaging a piece of fine china.
annotation.walkthrough: Imari is Japanese porcelain, named after the port it was shipped from.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the blue, red and gold Japanese ware takes its name from the port it was shipped from.

entries.clue: Humble, with endless resources (4)

indicators.note: a word with no end has lost its final letter

blocks.note: resources = one's funds or wealth, a five-letter word; cut its final S

annotation.surface: A modest person who has boundless wealth.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs humility with endless riches; the answer comes from means with its end removed. Mean here is the old sense of lowly, as in 'of mean birth'.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: 'of mean birth' is of low or lowly station, the opposite of noble.

entries.clue: One takes first bit of LSD at Burning Man we hear (9)

indicators.note: take only the opening letter
the phrase is heard, not read

blocks.note: an arsonist is a man who burns things

annotation.surface: A festival-goer takes a tab of acid at the Burning Man festival in the Nevada desert.
annotation.walkthrough: Burning Man is a real festival where drugs are not unknown, so 'takes' looks like taking a drug; it means steals.
annotation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits larceny, theft: one who takes.

entries.clue: A bit kept to one side (5)

blocks.note: a bit = a portion or piece of something

annotation.surface: A small portion is set aside for later.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one phrase; split it as 'A bit' for the wordplay and 'to one side' for the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Apart can mean aside, to one side, as in setting something apart.

entries.clue: Appearance of male lice, possibly, not new (13)

indicators.note: the N for 'new' is to be taken out

blocks.note: lice are one example of an infestation
N = new; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A man's head lice have turned up, perhaps not for the first time.
annotation.walkthrough: The N removed is the first N of INFESTATION.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ghost's showing, or a symptom's emergence, is an appearance.
